title: Every requirement, mapped
lede: Each requirement below comes from the official documents. Next to it: what QUERRA will do, and an honest status today. Nothing is marked in place without evidence.
checked: Documents checked on 7 November 2026: Open Call page, Annex 1 (Guidelines), Annex 1.1 (Technical Specification), Annex 2 (Proposal template), Annex 2.1 (F6S form), FAQ v1.0.

planned.label: Planned
planned.help: In the work plan; not done yet

decision.label: Decision needed
decision.help: The owner must choose or confirm

gap.label: Gap
gap.help: Known shortfall that must be closed

items.req: A sole applicant must be an incorporated SME, start-up or small mid-cap in an EU or associated country, with a valid VAT number
items.resp: Confirm QUERRA's legal entity, VAT number and SME status before submission

items.req: PIC number (or N/A)
items.resp: Register a PIC in the EU Participant Register

items.req: Starting maturity of at least TRL4
items.resp: TRL4 evidence pack targeted for 28 Nov 2026, described inside the proposal

items.req: Exactly one topic
items.resp: T4: smart and predictive pest and disease management

items.req: One proposal per entity; no double funding; no conflict of interest with the Nostradamus consortium
items.resp: Choose any second partner only after checking links to consortium partners (e.g. ECoE)

items.req: Official template, at most 20 pages, Calibri 11, English, PDF; the proposal must be self-contained
items.resp: Key figures and evidence go inside the PDF; this website is not relied on by evaluators

items.req: Submit on F6S by 2 Dec 2026, 17:00 CET; at most €50,000; fixed 12 months
items.resp: Budget and plan built for 12 months and within the cap

items.req: Choosing T4 commits the project to use Module M4 and its datasets
items.resp: The scouting round is driven by M4 risk and crop-stage outputs and checks them in the field (see The M4 loop)

items.req: M4 outputs are open, but its models are proprietary to ECoE
items.resp: Consume outputs only; never re-implement or redistribute M4 models

items.req: Build on needs identified through the Multi-Actor Platforms (MAPs) and surveys
items.resp: Co-design with the primary site's MAP in Sprint 2; trace each input to a requirement

items.req: Decision support for farmers, advisors and cooperatives that reduces administrative burden
items.resp: Structured, reviewed field records replace ad-hoc notes; the app records decisions and never prescribes

items.req: One primary demonstration site (Cyprus or Germany for T4); the other is the paired secondary region
items.resp: Choose the primary site. Cyprus is M4's development site with weekly in-situ stress observations; Germany is M4's replication site

items.req: Implement and compare edge, cloud and mixed solutions
items.resp: Run the same workflow in all three set-ups and measure latency, energy, data volume and losses

items.req: Edge components keep working offline and buffer data locally with no loss
items.resp: Capture and inference already run on the Jetson; local buffering and sync are planned
items.evidence: Inference on the device: engineer report, export pending

items.req: Sync with lightweight protocols (MQTT; CoAP in development)
items.resp: Publish compact observation records to the IoT Observatory over MQTT

items.req: Assess and document the energy and performance trade-off across architectures
items.resp: Measure energy per observation and bytes sent on the field unit for each architecture

items.req: Portable across execution options A–C (containers, pinned dependencies, no hard-coded endpoints)
items.resp: OCI container with a lock file and external configuration

items.req: Data Cube work in Python inside Cube-in-a-Box, using dc.load
items.resp: M4 and EO context loaded through dc.load in the reference container

items.req: IoT data only through the IoT Observatory Python SDK
items.resp: Read the site's weather and soil streams, and publish observations, through the SDK

items.req: EO discovery through the STAC catalogue, signed URLs and cloud-native partial reads
items.resp: Replace the current public Sentinel-2 replay with STAC queries to the Nostradamus catalogue

items.req: State which Nostradamus data interfaces are used and why
items.resp: EO pipelines (context), Data Cube (M4 outputs), IoT Observatory (site weather and soil; our observations)

items.req: FAIR data, REST APIs, OGC/ISO standards, INSPIRE metadata, AGROVOC/GEMET vocabularies
items.resp: GeoJSON/CSV observation records with AGROVOC terms and EPPO codes; documented REST endpoints

items.req: AI model outputs in open formats (e.g. ONNX)
items.resp: Export the model to ONNX; TensorRT is only used as an on-device accelerator

items.req: External datasets are documented in the Nostradamus Data Dictionary and shared after the project
items.resp: Data Dictionary entries for every external source, including NASA POWER

items.req: Public repository under an OSI licence, with installation, API and dependency documentation
items.resp: Public repository from Sprint 1 under an OSI licence such as Apache-2.0

items.req: No personal data, credentials, tokens or keys in repositories
items.resp: Privacy checks are already enforced for this site (no GPS, no coordinates); the same checks apply to the app repository

items.req: No proprietary dependency that prevents integration unless justified
items.resp: TensorRT is proprietary: justify it as an edge accelerator and ship an ONNX Runtime fallback

items.req: Python or supported tools, version control, integration tests against Nostradamus APIs
items.resp: Python pipelines with tests against the Data Cube and IoT Observatory interfaces

items.req: At least 10 h of training, proof of connection, use-case brief, kick-off item, monthly posts, project profile
items.resp: Planned in Sprint 1

items.req: Design report with stakeholder input and a deployment strategy signed off by mentors
items.resp: Planned in Sprint 2

items.req: Implementation, documentation and validation reports, a demo video, structured validation datasets, one podcast appearance
items.resp: Planned in Sprint 3

items.req: On-site demo and training with at least 10 attendees; training package; at least 40 survey responses; an EIP-AGRI practice abstract; exploitation plan; video
items.resp: Planned in Sprint 4; the 40 survey responses need outreach beyond the demo day

items.req: Field-tested evidence for at least one target; for T4, a >40% reduction in pesticide use
items.resp: Paired-plot comparison of loop-guided versus standard decisions, to agree with the site partner

items.req: Desk-based transferability to the secondary region using its Data Cube, EO and IoT streams
items.resp: Re-run the pipeline on the paired site's data; document differences in climate, soil and connectivity

items.req: Reach TRL7 at a Nostradamus site with real end users by month 12
items.resp: An operational scouting round with farmers and advisors at the primary site

items.req: Contribution to the expected impacts of the Horizon Europe Cluster 6 destination
items.resp: To be written in the proposal

items.req: Trustworthy AI: transparency, explainability, bias mitigation
items.resp: Uncertainty shown, abstention routed to people, group-aware splits and reviewer disagreement kept; model card planned
items.evidence: Design shown in How it learns

items.req: Gender balance of the team (scored, and the last tie-breaker)
items.resp: Name the team and its gender balance in Table 3 of the template

items.req: Accessible interface for users with lower digital skills or limited hardware
items.resp: Large-target, offline-first field interface; local-language labels for end users

items.req: Data protection
items.resp: Farm locations stay private; personal data is minimised; site and repository privacy checks

items.req: Realistic budget: equipment as depreciation only, no subcontracting, 25% indirect costs; capacity to pre-finance until sprint approval
items.resp: To be detailed in Tables 5–6
